entries.content: Social notes for Brightside Fixtures: pillar targets agreed in June are Educate 40 / Authority 25 / Connection 20 / Promotion 15. Branded tag #BrightsideBuilt. Showroom open Saturdays. Persona slugs: marcus (trade contractor, avt_marcus_01). Links go in the first comment on LinkedIn and Facebook with utm_medium=social.

testimonials.content: I stopped scheduling a call-back week. Eighteen months on the Harlow Street doors and not one has lifted.
The kitchen looks the same as the day it went in.

department.preamble: Brightside social here. Three variants on the finish-schedule brief for Marcus at Problem Aware, Educate pillar, proof from the finish-schedule handbook page and the Harlow Street grid. Self-scored below; you are the second reader. Links sit in the first comment on both platforms, the X version is omitted because the persona does not read X, and the Facebook variant carries a plain proof photo from the library rather than a designed card.

drafts.content: Stop asking your cabinet shop for a third coat. Two coats keyed with 320 grit outlast four that are not, and the 41 Harlow Street doors are 18 months in with zero call-backs. If you want to elevate the finish on a working kitchen, ask what happened between the coats, not how many there were. Save this for the next finish schedule you sign.
drafts.first_comment: The finish schedule we follow, coat by coat: https://brightsidefixtures.example/finish-schedule?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social

drafts.content: Myth: the lacquer failed. Truth: the coat under it was never sanded. Of 312 doors through our finish room in July, the 4 that came back had skipped the 320 pass between coats on one rush order. The 41 Harlow Street doors got the pass and are 18 months in with zero call-backs. Ask your shop what happens between coats, then save this for the next finish schedule you sign.
drafts.first_comment: The finish schedule, coat by coat, with flash times for a Texas August: https://brightsidefixtures.example/finish-schedule?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social

drafts.content: We used to skip the sand between coats on rush jobs. Then 4 doors from one July kitchen came back with the top coat lifting at the seams, and the fix cost more than the day we saved. Every coat gets the 320 pass now, rush or not, and the 41 Harlow Street doors are 18 months in with zero call-backs. Comment with the finish failure you see most and we will answer it in the next post.

alternatives.content: 4 of 312 doors came back in July. All four skipped the 320 pass between coats on one rush order; the other 308 are in kitchens. The number that predicts a call-back is the grit between coats, not the coat count.
